notes: IFRS in every year 2007-2025, EUR, fiscal year ending 31 December. All 19 years FY2007-FY2025 were found in adidas's own annual reports; no year or field is missing.

Scope break (Reebok): FY2007-FY2019 are consolidated totals including the Reebok business. From Q1 2021 Reebok was reclassified to discontinued operations and the sale closed on 1 March 2022, so FY2020 and FY2021 revenue, operating profit and total assets are the continuing-operations figures (ex-Reebok) used in adidas's later ten-year overviews. FY2020 is therefore shown as revenue 18,435 / operating profit 746 (continuing) instead of the 19,844 / 751 first published in the 2020 annual report, and is flagged restated; its net income attributable (432, EPS 2.21) is the 2020 annual report figure including a +13m gain from discontinued operations (prior-year divestments), and balance-sheet items are as reported (Reebok was not yet held for sale at 31 December 2020). Part of the apparent 2019-to-2020 revenue drop (23,640 -> 18,435) is this scope change, not a like-for-like decline.

FY2016 revenue and operating profit (18,483 / 1,582) are the continuing-operations figures restated in the 2018 and 2025 ten-year overviews after the 2017 divestiture of TaylorMade, Adams Golf, Ashworth and CCM Hockey; the 2016 annual report itself showed 19,291 / 1,491. FY2011 is the IAS 8 restatement published in the 2012 report (revenue 13,322 vs 13,344; net income attributable 613 vs 671). FY2017 balance-sheet figures are the IAS 8 restatement of the 2018 report.

netIncome is net income attributable to shareholders, i.e. including discontinued operations: FY2021 includes a EUR 666m gain from the Reebok discontinued operation and FY2022 a EUR 384m gain, so those two years are not comparable with the continuing-operations figures shown in adidas's own overviews (2021: 1,492; 2022: 254).

dilutedEPS is the diluted EPS from continuing and discontinued operations so that it ties to netIncome (e.g. 2025: 7.51, 2022: 3.34, 2021: 10.90). adidas's ten-year overviews instead print EPS and net income excluding the goodwill impairments of FY2012-FY2015 (265 / 52 / 78 / 34 million) and the FY2017 one-off tax charge of EUR 76m, which is why the overview rows differ from the reported statements used here (e.g. FY2015 overview: net income 668 and EPS 3.54 vs reported 634 and 3.15; FY2017 overview: 1,173 and 7.00 vs reported 1,097 and 5.38).

operatingIncome is the reported operating profit of the consolidated income statement, i.e. after the goodwill impairment losses charged in FY2009-FY2015 where applicable (FY2012: 920 after 265; FY2013: 1,181 after 52; FY2014: 883 after 78; FY2015: 1,059 after 34).

totalDebt is the sum of the published balance-sheet lines short-term borrowings + long-term borrowings + current and non-current lease liabilities (identical to the 'composition of adjusted net borrowings' note less pensions and factoring). IFRS 16 was applied from 1 January 2019 without restating 2018, so totalDebt jumps from 1,675 (2018) to 4,770 (2019) purely because leases came on balance sheet; pre-2019 operating leases were off balance sheet. Lease-free gross borrowings for 2025 are EUR 2,642m (2024: 2,485m).

capex is purchases of property, plant and equipment only, stored negative; adidas reports purchases of intangible assets separately (2025: 114, 2024: 121, 2023: 141, 2022: 191, 2021: 173, 2020: 64, 2019: 110, 2018: 96, 2017: 74, 2016: 65, 2015: 49, 2014: 49, 2013: 52, 2012: 58, 2011: 58, 2010: 42, 2009: 46, 2008: 60, 2007: 55 million). Yahoo Finance's capex figure adds intangibles, which is why Yahoo's 2025 capex (about EUR 478m) differs from the 363m reported here.

operatingCashFlow is the consolidated total including discontinued operations as presented in the cash flow statement (2021: 3,192m = 2,873m + 320m; 2020: 1,486m = 1,489m - 3m). FY2023 and FY2022 are the figures adjusted for IAS 29 hyperinflation accounting as published in the following year's report, hence restated = true: FY2023 2,550m in the 2024 annual report (the 2023 annual report showed 2,630m), FY2022 -479m in the 2023 annual report (=-394m continuing -85m discontinued; the 2022 annual report itself showed -543m = -458m - 85m).

dividendPerShare is the dividend for the reporting year as printed in adidas's ten-year overview. FY2019 is nil: the EUR 3.85 proposed for 2019 was withdrawn when the COVID-19 syndicated loan suspended dividend payments and no dividend was paid in 2020. FY2025 (EUR 2.80) was still subject to AGM approval when the 2025 annual report was published.

sharesOutstanding is the number of shares outstanding at year-end (in thousands in the source, converted to units). FY2019 employees 65,194 is the restated count including temporary contracts of up to six months (originally 59,333).

Cross-check against Yahoo Finance (docs/global-companies/snapshot-2026-10-26.json) for the last four years: the snapshot converts the P&L and cash flow at average month-end rates and the balance sheet at the closing rate, so each USD figure has to be divided by the rate that fits its year. Taking the rate implied by Yahoo's own gross profit (2025: 1.1324, 2024: 1.0802, 2023: 1.0847, 2022: 1.0517), revenue comes out at 24,810 / 23,686 / 21,428 / 22,511m EUR against 24,811 / 23,683 / 21,427 / 22,511m reported and net income at 1,340 / 764 / -75 / 612m against 1,340 / 764 / -75 / 612m reported - every line within 0.1%. Yahoo's operatingIncome is also within 0.3% (2025: 2,061 vs 2,056). Two confirmations of the figures used here: Yahoo's operating cash flow converts to -479m for FY2022 and 2,550m for FY2023, i.e. the hyperinflation-adjusted values, and its capex converts to 477 / 540 / 504 / 695m, exactly purchases of PP&E plus intangibles in those years. Balance-sheet items convert at the closing rate and match too (2025: total assets 20,262, equity 5,776, total debt 5,555 vs 5,554 reported), except cash: Yahoo shows 1,520m for FY2025 against adidas's 1,617m and 1,812m for FY2022 against 798m reported, so its cash line is a different definition.
